content.shloka:
Varnaanam Artha-Sanghaanaam Rasaanaam Chhandasaam Api |
Mangalaanam Cha Kartaarau Vande Vaani Vinaayakau ||
content.meaning: I bow to Goddess Saraswati (Vaani) and Lord Ganesha (Vinayaka), who are the creators of all letters, meanings, sentiments, poetic metres, and all auspiciousness.
content.transliteration:
Varṇānām Artha-Saṅghānāṃ Rasānāṃ Chandasām Api |
Maṅgalānāṃ Ca Kartārau Vande Vāṇī Vināyakau ||

content.shloka:
Bhavaanee Shankarau Vande Shraddha Vishvaas Roopinau |
Yaabhyaam Vinaa Na Pashyanti Siddhaah Svaantahstham Eeshvaram ||
content.meaning: I salute Bhavani (Parvati) and Shankara (Shiva), who are the embodiments of faith and belief. Without these two (faith and belief), even the siddhas (accomplished sages) cannot perceive the Lord dwelling in their own hearts.
content.transliteration:
Bhavānī Śaṅkarau Vande Śraddhā Viśvāsa Rūpiṇau |
Yābhyāṃ Vinā Na Paśyanti Siddhāḥ Svāntahsthaṃ Īśvaram ||

content.shloka:
Vandey Bodhamayam Nityam Gurum Shankar Roopinam |
Yamaashrito Hi Vakropi Chandrah Sarvatra Vandyate ||
content.meaning: I salute the Guru, who is the embodiment of wisdom eternal and is the form of Shankara (Shiva) Himself. By taking refuge in whom, even the crooked moon becomes universally revered.
content.transliteration:
Vande Bodhamayaṃ Nityaṃ Guruṃ Śaṅkara Rūpiṇam |
Yamāśrito Hi Vakropi Candraḥ Sarvatra Vandyate ||

content.shloka:
Seetaa Raama Guna Grama Punya Aranya Vihaarinaau |
Vande Vishudddha Vignaanau Kavishvar Kapishvarau ||
content.meaning: I salute both Valmiki (the king of poets) and Hanuman (the king of monkeys), who are repositories of pure wisdom and who delight in wandering through the sacred forest of Sita and Rama's virtues.
content.transliteration:
Sītā Rāma Guṇa Grāma Puṇya Araṇya Vihāriṇau |
Vande Viśuddha Vijñānau Kavīśvara Kapīśvarau ||

content.shloka:
Udabhava Sthiti Samhaar Kaarineem Klesha Haarineem |
Sarva Shreyaskareem Seetaam Nato'ham Raam Vallabhaam ||
content.meaning: I bow to Sita, beloved of Rama, who is the cause of creation, preservation, and dissolution, who removes all afflictions, and who bestows all that is supremely auspicious.
content.transliteration:
Udbhava Sthiti Saṃhāra Kāriṇīṃ Kleśa Hāriṇīm |
Sarva Śreyaskarīṃ Sītāṃ Nato’ham Rāma Vallabhām ||

content.shloka:
Naanaa Puraan Nigamaagam Sammatam Yad Raamaayaney Nigaditam Kvachidanyatopi |
Svantah Sukhay Tulasee Raghunath Gaathaa Bhaashaa Nibandhamatimanjulamaatanoti ||
content.meaning: That which is established in various Puranas, Vedas, and Agamas, and narrated in the Ramayana and elsewhere too -- Tulsidas composes this most beautiful narrative of Lord Raghunath in the vernacular language (Awadhi), for the delight of his own heart.
content.transliteration:
Nānā Purāṇa Nigāmāgama Sammataṃ Yad Rāmāyaṇe Nigaditaṃ Kvacidanyatopi |
Svāntah Sukhāya Tulasī Raghunātha Gāthā Bhāṣā Nibandham Atimañjulam Ātanoti ||

content.shloka:
Shankaram Shankaraachaarya Keertim Cha Shankaram Mama |
Bhooshanaam Bhuvanaasyaapi Shankaram Pranato'smyaham ||
content.meaning: I bow to Shankara (Shiva), who is Shankaracharya (the one who bestows auspiciousness), who is my fame and auspiciousness, and who is the ornament of the entire world.
content.transliteration:
Śaṅkaraṃ Śaṅkarācārya Kīrtim Ca Śaṅkaraṃ Mama |
Bhūṣaṇaṃ Bhuvanasyāpi Śaṅkaraṃ Praṇato’smyaham ||

content.shloka:
Jo Sumirat Sidhi Hoye Gananayak Karibara Badana |
Karau Anugraha Soye Buddhi Raasi Subha Guna Sadana ||
content.meaning: He whose very remembrance brings success, whose face is like that of a great elephant -- may that Ganesh, who is the treasure-house of wisdom and the abode of all auspicious virtues, bestow his grace upon me.
content.transliteration:
Jo Sumirat Siddhi Hoi Gaṇanāyaka Karibara Badana |
Karau Anugraha Soi Buddhi Rāśi Śubha Guṇa Sadana ||

content.shloka:
Raghukul Reet Sadaa Chali Aaee |
Praan Jaaye Par Vachan Na Jaaee ||
content.meaning: It has always been the tradition of the Raghu dynasty -- one may give up one's life, but never one's word.
content.transliteration:
Raghukula Rīti Sadā Calī Āī |
Prāṇa Jāi Para Vacana Na Jāī ||

content.shloka:
Hari Ananta Hari Kathaa Anantaa |
Kahahin Sunahein Bahu Bidhi Sab Santaa ||
content.meaning: Lord Hari is infinite and so are the stories of Lord Hari. All the saints narrate and listen to them in many ways.
content.transliteration:
Hari Ananta Hari Kathā Anantā |
Kahahin Sunahin Bahu Vidhi Saba Santā ||

content.shloka:
Bhaye Pragat Kripaalaa Deen Dayaalaa Kausalyaa Hitkaari |
Harshit Mahataaree Muni Man Haari Adbhut Roop Bichaari ||
content.meaning: The gracious and compassionate Lord, the benefactor of Kausalya, manifested Himself. Beholding His wondrous form, the delighted mother and the sages were captivated in their hearts.
content.transliteration:
Bhae Pragaṭa Kṛpālā Dīna Dayālā Kausalya Hitkārī |
Harṣita Mahatārī Muni Mana Hārī Adbhuta Rūpa Bicārī ||

content.shloka:
Bigat Moha Mana Ram Pad Dekhey |
Raam Roop Anoopam Avalekhey ||
content.meaning: Beholding the feet of Lord Rama, the delusion of the mind vanished. The form of Rama is incomparably beautiful and indescribable.
content.transliteration:
Vigata Moha Mana Rāma Pada Dekhe |
Rāma Rūpa Anūpama Avalekhe ||

content.shloka:
Sab Nar Karahin Paraspar Preetee |
Chalahin Svadharma Nirat Shruti Reetee ||
content.meaning: All people showed mutual love and affection toward one another. Everyone walked the path of their own dharma, devoted to the ways laid down in the Vedas.
content.transliteration:
Saba Nara Karahin Paraspara Prītī |
Calahin Svadharma Nirata Śruti Rītī ||

content.shloka:
Naahin Daridra Kau Dukhi Na Deenaa |
Naahin Kau Ajna Na Lachhan Heenaa ||
content.meaning: No one was poor, sorrowful, or wretched. No one was ignorant or devoid of good qualities.
content.transliteration:
Nāhin Daridra Kau Dukhī Na Dīnā |
Nāhin Kau Ajña Na Lacchana Hīnā ||

content.shloka:
Hara Giri Mandir Sundara Bana Baagaa |
Nadee Naav Sar Sahaj Taraagaa ||
content.meaning: On Shiva's mountain (Kailasa), there are beautiful temples, groves, and gardens, and rivers, lakes, and ponds with their natural waves.
content.transliteration:
Hara Giri Mandira Sundara Bana Bāgā |
Nadī Nāva Sara Sahaja Tarāgā ||

content.shloka:
Siya Raam Mein Sab Jag Jaanee |
Karahu Pranaam Jori Jug Paanee ||
content.meaning: Know that the entire world resides in Sita and Rama. Bow to them with folded hands.
content.transliteration:
Siyā Rāma Mein Saba Jaga Jānī |
Karahu Praṇāma Jori Juga Pānī ||

content.shloka:
Dheeraj Dharma Mitra Aru Naaree |
Aapad Kaal Parikhi-ah Chaaree ||
content.meaning: Patience, righteousness, a friend, and a wife -- these four are truly tested in times of adversity.
content.transliteration:
Dhīraja Dharma Mitra Aru Nārī |
Āpada Kāla Parikhīaha Cārī ||

content.shloka:
Jaake Priya Na Raam Baidehee |
Taji-ah Tahi Koti Bairee Sam Ehee ||
content.meaning: One to whom Rama and Sita are not dear, abandon such a person as you would a million enemies.
content.transliteration:
Jāke Priya Na Rāma Vaidehī |
Tajiyaha Tahi Koṭi Bairī Sama Ehī ||

content.shloka:
Parivartini Samsaare Mritah Ko Na Mriyate Punah |
Sa Jaato Yena Jaatena Yaati Vamshah Samunnatim ||
content.meaning: In this revolving world, who that has died does not die again? Truly born is he alone by whose birth his entire lineage rises to greatness.
content.transliteration:
Parivartini Saṃsāre Mṛtah Ko Na Mriyate Punah |
Sa Jāto Yena Jātena Yāti Vaṃśah Samunnatim ||

content.shloka:
Binu Satsanga Bibeka Na Hoee |
Raam Kripa Binu Sulabh Na Soee ||
content.meaning: Without the company of saints, true discernment (viveka) does not arise. And without the grace of Rama, such holy company is not easily obtained.
content.transliteration:
Binu Satsaṅga Viveka Na Hoī |
Rāma Kṛpā Binu Sulabha Na Soī ||

content.shloka:
Param Dharma Shruti Bidita Ahinsaa |
Par Nirantar Jeevan Jinsaa ||
content.meaning: Non-violence is the supreme dharma, as proclaimed by the Vedas. Compassion for all living beings at all times is its essence.
content.transliteration:
Parama Dharma Śruti Vidita Ahiṃsā |
Para Nirantara Jīvana Jiṃsā ||

content.shloka:
Ek Bharat Bhal Lok Bikhyaata |
Prem Prateeti Sabahin Mana Jaata ||
content.meaning: Bharat was well-known in the world for his goodness. His love and sincerity were recognized by all hearts.
content.transliteration:
Eka Bharata Bhala Loka Vikhyāta |
Prema Pratīti Sabahin Mana Jātā ||

content.shloka:
Hari Tav Kripa Bhalu Mohi Na Maayaa |
Nath Sakala Saadhana Mai Aapaayaa ||
content.meaning: O Lord Hari, by Your grace I remain untouched by Maya. O Master, I have attained all spiritual means through You.
content.transliteration:
Hari Tava Kṛpā Bhalu Mohi Na Māyā |
Nātha Sakala Sādhana Mai Āpāyā ||

content.shloka:
Bharatahi Hoye Na Raajamadu Bidhi Hari Hara Pad Paaye |
Kabanahu Lobh Na Bhulaheen Raam Charann Chitt Laaye ||
content.meaning: Even if Bharat were to attain the positions of Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva, he would not be intoxicated by royal power. He can never be led astray by greed, for his mind is fixed on the feet of Rama.
content.transliteration:
Bharatahi Hoi Na Rājamadu Vidhi Hari Hara Pada Pāi |
Kabahū Lobha Na Bhūlahin Rāma Caraṇa Citta Lāi ||

content.shloka:
Tulsee Jabahi Raam Kau Bhajaa |
Janm Maran Kau Shok Tajaa ||
content.meaning: Tulsidas says, the moment one worships Rama, the sorrow of birth and death is abandoned.
content.transliteration:
Tulasī Jabahi Rāma Kau Bhajā |
Janma Maraṇa Kau Śoka Tajā ||

content.shloka:
Nirmal Mana Jana So Mohi Paavaa |
Mohi Kapatat Chhal Chhidra Na Bhaavaa ||
content.meaning: He who has a pure heart finds Me. Deceit, trickery, and fault-finding are not pleasing to Me.
content.transliteration:
Nirmala Mana Jana So Mohi Pāvā |
Mohi Kapaṭa Chala Chidra Na Bhāvā ||

content.shloka:
Masak Samaana Roop Kapi Dhaaree |
Lankhini Hanaa Laath Tehraaree ||
content.meaning: Hanuman assumed a form as tiny as a mosquito. He then struck Lanka's guardian demoness (Lankhini) with a single kick.
content.transliteration:
Masaka Samāna Rūpa Kapi Dhārī |
Laṅkhinī Hanā Lātha Tehrārī ||

content.shloka:
Param Dharma Shruti Bidita Ahinsaa |
Par Nirandha Jiiv Jinsaa ||
content.meaning: The supreme dharma, as declared by the Vedas, is non-violence -- treating every living being with constant compassion.
content.transliteration:
Parama Dharma Śruti Vidita Ahiṃsā |
Para Nirandha Jīva Jiṃsā ||

content.shloka:
Prabhu Pragat Bhe Sab Muni Sukhkaaree |
Anuj Sahit Karunaa Aalakaaree ||
content.meaning: The Lord appeared, bringing joy to all the sages, accompanied by His younger brother (Lakshman), the very embodiment of compassion.
content.transliteration:
Prabhu Pragaṭa Bhe Saba Muni Sukhkārī |
Anuja Sahita Karuṇā Alakārī ||

content.shloka:
Moorhi Hridaya So Nahin Sansehaa |
Mohe Saba Para Sambhava Ehaa ||
content.meaning: There is no doubt in the heart of a wise person. Such equanimity toward all is indeed possible for Me.
content.transliteration:
Mūṛhi Hṛdaya So Nāhin Saṃśehā |
Mohe Saba Para Sambhava Ehā ||

content.shloka:
Sab Ke Mamtaa Raam Par Nekey |
Lakhi Patu Raakhi Dehee Ek Tekey ||
content.meaning: Everyone's loving attachment to Rama was truly profound. Seeing this, even their bodies were sustained solely by that devotion.
content.transliteration:
Saba Ke Mamatā Rāma Para Neke |
Lakhi Paṭu Rākhi Dehī Eka Teke ||

content.shloka:
Khala Bans Paalahi Jo Sansaaraa |
Te Nar Paas Na Aavahin Maaraa ||
content.meaning: Those who nurture wickedness in the world -- such people do not find a way to reach Me.
content.transliteration:
Khala Baṃśa Pālahi Jo Saṃsārā |
Te Nara Pāsa Na Āvahin Mārā ||

content.shloka:
Bali Beera Bar Banar |
Chalo Jaai Raghuveera Pukaar ||
content.meaning: Bali was a brave and mighty monkey. He went forth at the call of the Hero of the Raghu dynasty.
content.transliteration:
Bāli Vīra Bara Bānara |
Calo Jāi Raghuvīra Pukāra ||

content.shloka:
Ek Bar Chupesare Jaayee |
Sugriv Sen Samet Sabhaayee ||
content.meaning: Once, going secretly, Sugriva assembled with his entire army at the gathering.
content.transliteration:
Eka Bāra Cupesare Jāī |
Sugrīva Sena Sameta Sabhāī ||

content.shloka:
Nij Bhuja Bala Raghubeera Bharosaa |
Jeetey Sakala Bishwa Koi Khosaa ||
content.meaning: With the strength of one's own arms and faith in Raghuveer (Rama), the whole world can be conquered. Who can take that away?
content.transliteration:
Nija Bhuja Bala Raghuvīra Bharosā |
Jīte Sakala Viśva Koi Khosā ||

content.shloka:
Sunat Binay Sunder Kapi Baanee |
Raam Kripa Aaee Anugaanee ||
content.meaning: Hearing the beautiful and humble words of the monkey (Hanuman), the grace of Rama was made manifest.
content.transliteration:
Sunata Vinaya Sundara Kapi Bānī |
Rāma Kṛpā Āī Anugānī ||

content.shloka:
Gaye Raam Binu Kahi Nahi Thoore |
Chale Sakala Bana Khojat Teeraa ||
content.meaning: Without Rama there is no rest anywhere. All of them set out, searching every corner of the forest.
content.transliteration:
Gae Rāma Binu Kahi Nahī Thūre |
Cale Sakala Bana Khojata Tīrā ||

content.shloka:
Kapi Saagara Dekhahu Apaaraa |
Paar Karo Koi Buddhi Vichaaraa ||
content.meaning: Behold the boundless ocean, O monkeys! Think of some plan to cross to the other side.
content.transliteration:
Kapi Sāgara Dekhahu Apārā |
Pāra Karo Koī Buddhi Vicārā ||

content.shloka:
Hari Ichha Sab Kavan Badaayee |
Raghupati Kahuun Sakala Sachaaee ||
content.meaning: All happens by the will of God -- what is there to boast about? Rama spoke the complete truth.
content.transliteration:
Hari Icchā Saba Kavana Baḍāī |
Raghupati Kahūṁ Sakala Sacāī ||

content.shloka:
Sab Sukh Bhajan Tumhaar |
Raam Kripa Baarishu Dhaar ||
content.meaning: All happiness lies in Your worship, O Lord. The grace of Rama rains down in torrents.
content.transliteration:
Saba Sukha Bhajana Tumhāra |
Rāma Kṛpā Bāriṣhu Dhāra ||

content.shloka:
Jaambuvant Ke Bachan Suhaaye |
Suni Hanumat Hridaya Ati Bhaaye ||
content.meaning: The delightful words of Jambuvant were heard by Hanuman, and they greatly pleased his heart.
content.transliteration:
Jāmbuvanta Ke Bacana Suhāe |
Suni Hanumāna Hṛdaya Ati Bhāe ||

content.shloka:
Ram Kaaju Keenhey Binu Mohee |
Kahe Na Kaal Binu Jaaye Sohee ||
content.meaning: Until I have accomplished the work of Lord Rama, even Time (Death) cannot overcome me.
content.transliteration:
Rāma Kāju Kīnhe Binu Mohī |
Kahe Na Kāla Binu Jāi Sohī ||

content.shloka:
Paavan Naam Binu Ek Adhaaraa |
Taran Tar Hanumat Tihaaraa ||
content.meaning: Your holy name alone is the sole support. Hanuman, You are the one who ferries (devotees) across.
content.transliteration:
Pāvana Nāma Binu Eka Adhārā |
Taraṇa Tara Hanumāta Tihārā ||

content.shloka:
Raam Doota Atulita Bal Dhaamaa |
Anjani Putra Pavan Sut Naamaa ||
content.meaning: He is the messenger of Rama and the repository of incomparable strength. He is the son of Anjani and is known as the son of the Wind-god.
content.transliteration:
Rāma Dūta Atulita Bala Dhāmā |
Añjanī Putra Pavana Suta Nāmā ||

content.shloka:
Naasai Rog Harai Sab Peeraa |
Japat Nirantar Hanumant Beeraa ||
content.meaning: All diseases are destroyed and all suffering is removed by constantly chanting the name of brave Hanuman.
content.transliteration:
Nāsai Roga Harai Saba Pīrā |
Japata Nirantara Hanumānta Bīrā ||

content.shloka:
Jai Jai Jai Hanumaan Gosaaee |
Kripa Karahu Gurudev Ki Naayee ||
content.meaning: Victory, victory, victory to Lord Hanuman! Bestow your grace upon me as would a revered Guru.
content.transliteration:
Jai Jai Jai Hanumāna Gosāī |
Kṛpā Karahu Gurudeva Kī Nāī ||

content.shloka:
Ashta Siddhi Nav Nidhi Ke Daata |
As Bar Deen Jaanaki Maata ||
content.meaning: Mother Janaki (Sita) has granted you the boon of being the bestower of the eight supernatural powers (siddhis) and the nine treasures (nidhis).
content.transliteration:
Aṣṭa Siddhi Nava Nidhi Ke Dātā |
Asa Bara Dīna Jānakī Mātā ||

content.shloka:
Sab Par Raam Tapasvi Raajaa |
Tinhi Ke Kaaj Sakal Tum Saajaa ||
content.meaning: Rama, the great ascetic king, is above all. You (Hanuman) accomplish all His tasks.
content.transliteration:
Saba Para Rāma Tapasvī Rājā |
Tinhi Ke Kāja Sakala Tuma Sājā ||

content.shloka:
Sankat Te Hanumaan Chhudaave |
Mana Krama Bachan Dhyaan Jo Laave ||
content.meaning: Hanuman rescues from all calamities those who meditate upon him in thought, deed, and word.
content.transliteration:
Saṅkaṭa Te Hanumāna Chuḍāve |
Mana Krama Bacana Dhyāna Jo Lāve ||

content.shloka:
Ravan Rathanee Virath Raghuveeraa |
Dekhi Vibheeshan Bhayau Adheeraa ||
content.meaning: Ravana was on his chariot while Raghuveer (Rama) was without one. Seeing this, Vibhishana became anxious.
content.transliteration:
Rāvaṇa Rathanī Viratha Raghuvīrā |
Dekhi Vibhīṣaṇa Bhayau Adhīrā ||

content.shloka:
Sunu Saaranee Sab Kariyah Naaraa |
Yah Ravan Kaah Samara Haankaaraa ||
content.meaning: Listen, O charioteer, let everyone shout the war cry. What is Ravana's arrogance in battle worth?
content.transliteration:
Sunu Sāraṇī Saba Kariyaha Nārā |
Yaha Rāvaṇa Kāha Samara Haṅkārā ||

content.shloka:
Sauraja Dharama Na Charhat Raghuvansee |
Hridaya Basahu Kosalpur Vaasee ||
content.meaning: The descendants of Raghu never abandon valor and righteousness. The Lord of Ayodhya ever dwells in the heart.
content.transliteration:
Sauraja Dharama Na Carahata Raghuvaṃśī |
Hṛdaya Basahu Kosalapura Vāsī ||

content.shloka:
Nij Dal Bical Suru Gana Khaaya |
Dekhey Biraath Ravan Ris Aaya ||
content.meaning: Seeing his own army in disarray and the gods being devoured (metaphorically), Ravana without his chariot was filled with fury.
content.transliteration:
Nija Dala Vikala Sura Gaṇa Khāyā |
Dekhe Virātha Rāvaṇa Risa Āyā ||

content.shloka:
Prabhu Pratap Bali Sabui Gaye Maare |
Tamasa Loka Sahit Parivaare ||
content.meaning: By the might of the Lord's glory, all the mighty demons were slain, along with their entire clans, and sent to the realm of darkness.
content.transliteration:
Prabhu Pratāpa Bali Sabui Gae Māre |
Tamasa Loka Sahita Parivāre ||

content.shloka:
Raama Baana Rabi Ujiyaaraa |
Tamasa Milaa Ek Chhaar ||
content.meaning: The arrow of Rama shone like the sun. Darkness was reduced to mere dust.
content.transliteration:
Rāma Bāṇa Rabi Ujiyārā |
Tamasa Milā Eka Chāra ||

content.shloka:
Hoye Jayee Raam Ki Aayee |
Suranha Keenh Pushpavrishti Bhaayee ||
content.meaning: Victory came as the grace of Lord Rama arrived. The gods rained flowers in joy.
content.transliteration:
Hoe Jayī Rāma Kī Āī |
Suranha Kīnh Puṣpavṛṣṭi Bhāī ||

content.shloka:
Raam Kripa Kapi Man Deenhee |
Sab Bidhi Kusal Samajh Tab Keenhee ||
content.meaning: By the grace of Rama, the monkeys were given renewed courage. They then wisely accomplished all tasks in every way.
content.transliteration:
Rāma Kṛpā Kapi Mana Dīnhī |
Saba Vidhi Kuśala Samajha Taba Kīnhī ||

content.shloka:
Kaam Krodh Mad Lobh Sab Naath Narak Ke Panth |
Sab Parihari Raghuveerahi Bhajahu Bhajahu Bhagavant ||
content.meaning: Lust, anger, pride, and greed -- all are paths leading to hell. Abandon them all and worship Raghuveer (Rama), worship the Lord!
content.transliteration:
Kāma Krodha Mada Lobha Saba Nātha Naraka Ke Pantha |
Saba Parihari Raghuvīrahi Bhajahu Bhajahu Bhagavanta ||

content.shloka:
Ek Bhrosey Ek Bal Ek Aas Vishwaas |
Ek Raam Ghanashyaam Hit Chatak Tulseedaas ||
content.meaning: One reliance, one strength, one hope, one trust -- Tulsidas is like a Chatak bird, devoted solely to Rama, the dark-hued cloud of bliss.
content.transliteration:
Eka Bharose Eka Bala Eka Āsa Viśvāsa |
Eka Rāma Ghanashāma Hita Cātaka Tulasīdāsa ||

content.shloka:
Moh Sakala Byaadhina Kar Moolaa |
Tin Tey Puneeth Na Bhay Anukoolaa ||
content.meaning: Delusion is the root of all afflictions. From it, nothing holy or auspicious arises.
content.transliteration:
Moha Sakala Vyādhina Kara Mūlā |
Tina Te Punītha Na Bhaya Anukūlā ||

content.shloka:
Sumiri Pavanasut Paavan Naamoo |
Apane Basha Karahu Nija Kaamoo ||
content.meaning: Remember the holy name of the son of the Wind-god (Hanuman). Bring your desires under your own control.
content.transliteration:
Sumiri Pavanasuta Pāvana Nāmū |
Apane Vaśa Karahu Nija Kāmū ||

content.shloka:
Kaahey Ka Bhaya Dharahu Mana Maahin |
Jab Jag Karan Sahay Raam Naahin ||
content.meaning: Why do you harbor fear in your heart? When the cause and support of the entire world is Lord Rama Himself?
content.transliteration:
Kāhe Kā Bhaya Dharahu Mana Māhī |
Jaba Jaga Kāraṇa Sahāya Rāma Nāhī ||

content.shloka:
So Janeeyah Prabhu Bandhu Samaajar |
Jo Na Mitai Ati Aapada Kaajar ||
content.meaning: Know that person to be a true kinsman and companion of the Lord whose devotion does not waver even in the greatest adversity.
content.transliteration:
So Jānīyaha Prabhu Bandhu Samājāra |
Jo Na Miṭai Ati Āpada Kājara ||

content.shloka:
Bhaj Raam Charan Sukhadaaee |
Par Upakaar Bachan Man Kaaee ||
content.meaning: Worship the bliss-giving feet of Rama. Be of service to others in thought, word, and deed.
content.transliteration:
Bhaja Rāma Caraṇa Sukhadāī |
Para Upakāra Bacana Mana Kāī ||

content.shloka:
Mangal Bhavan Amangal Haaree |
Dravahu So Dashrath Ajir Bihaaree ||
content.meaning: He who is the abode of all auspiciousness and the destroyer of all that is inauspicious -- may that Lord, who sports in the courtyard of Dasharatha, be compassionate to us.
content.transliteration:
Maṅgala Bhavana Amaṅgala Hārī |
Dravahu So Daśaratha Ajira Bihārī ||
